correctness.rationale: For arbitrary d≥2,0≤r<d and all positive box widths, coordinate endpoint admissibility proves the exact membership criterion. A fixing deformation retract onto the surviving cubical r-skeleton and an explicit coordinate-face inclusion section prove the homotopy types, ranks, and all persistence epimorphisms. Gap/endpoint region partition yields the exact void polynomial; the positive leading term near the last width collision proves the extinction exponent and coefficient even with tied widths. The included standalone checker reproduced 50,114 exact finite assertions; its finite range does not replace the unrestricted argument.

value.rationale: The geometric skeleton and anisotropic box are natural test objects in the recently motivated finite-convexification problem. The theorem completely solves a continuous two-index-plus-weights family, including all homotopy changes, the full homology persistence barcode and the exact remaining-volume polynomial. Critical width ties yield a genuinely higher-order extinction phenomenon quantified by one positive binomial coefficient. This is beyond an existence result, a static cubical homology table, or an arbitrary unmotivated slice. The isotropic scalar threshold was already known; the value lies specifically in the full anisotropic persistence and positive tied-width volume-extinction structure.
